directive: **Structure** — the features are a dependency DAG (`bsc plan feature list` shows each feature + its `dependsOn`). PRESENT the dependency graph + roadmap and get the user's APPROVAL — there are no milestone phases and no phase numbering; sequencing is implied PURELY by each feature's `dependsOn`. Do NOT write phases.json or any issue files. Issues are generated from the features at GitHub-publish time, not during planning (no `bsc plan add`). Run `bsc plan feature list` to review the DAG, walk the user through the implied build order (foundations first — a feature builds after its `dependsOn` features), and resolve any cycle so the graph is acyclic. Leave no TODO/TBD/FIXME/XXX markers — the gate blocks on them. Where a real cross-feature contract exists (a shared schema/types/API), write it as a doc under `contracts/<name>.md` — the director owns those and workers read them as the source of truth. (Existing repos: inventory every screen/module first so none is missed.)

prompt:
The features are a dependency DAG — run `bsc plan feature list` to see every feature and its
`dependsOn`. PRESENT the dependency graph + roadmap and get the user's APPROVAL. There are no
milestone phases and no phase numbering: the build order is implied PURELY by each feature's
`dependsOn` (foundations first — a feature builds after the features it depends on). Do NOT write
phases.json or any issue files. Issues are generated from the features at GitHub-publish time, not
during planning (no `bsc plan add`).

Walk the user through the dependency graph:
1. Review the DAG with `bsc plan feature list` — confirm each feature's `dependsOn` is right and the
   graph is acyclic (a cycle holds the gate).
2. Present the implied roadmap — the build order the `dependsOn` edges describe (which features land
   first, what builds on what) — and get the user's APPROVAL.
Leave no TODO / TBD / FIXME / XXX markers — the gate blocks on them.

Where a real cross-feature contract exists (a shared schema/types/API), write it as a doc under
`contracts/<name>.md` — the director owns those and workers read them as the source of truth.
